subject: EN

explanation.body: Uhrzeiten werden meist im **12-Stunden-System** gesprochen (am = vormittags, pm = nachmittags). **half past ten** = 10:30 (nicht halb zehn!). **12 pm** = Mittag, **12 am** = Mitternacht. Die 0 wird **oh** gesprochen. Jahreszahlen zweigeteilt: 1917 = nineteen seventeen, aber 2009 = two thousand and nine.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Training Listening (Exkurs Uhrzeiten, Daten, Telefonnummern)

from.a: six pm / six in the evening
from.grund: Gesprochen wird im 12-Stunden-System: 18:00 = six pm.
half past ten = 10:30. Vorsicht: Im Deutschen wäre „halb elf“ 10:30, im Englischen heißt es half past **ten**.
21:15 = nine fifteen pm = quarter past nine in the evening.
Die 0 wird bei Uhrzeiten **oh** gesprochen: five oh-nine in the morning.
half past = eine halbe Stunde **nach** der genannten Stunde.
12 pm = Mittag, 12 am = Mitternacht.
12 am steht für 00:00 Uhr.

from.frage: Wie wird das Datum **1st May** gesprochen?
from.grund: Geschrieben 1st May → gesprochen the first of May.
Geschrieben May 1st → gesprochen May the first.
Jahreszahlen werden zweigeteilt: 19 | 17.
Zweigeteilt, die 0 als oh: eighteen oh-nine.
Ausnahme: 2009 = two thousand and nine.
v. Chr. = BC (Before Christ) oder BCE, wird **nach** der Zahl gesprochen.
n. Chr. = AD (Anno Domini), wird **vor** der Zahl gesprochen, oder CE nach der Zahl.

from.b: five hundred three, five hundred sixty-seven, …
from.grund: Telefonnummern werden Ziffer für Ziffer gesprochen, die 0 als **oh**, betont wird die letzte Ziffer jeder Gruppe.

from.frage: Wie wird die **0** in Telefonnummern meistens gesprochen?
from.grund: Bei Telefon- und Kontonummern sagt man meistens oh.

Ben is fascinated by history and old buildings.
Museum Island and the old palace

Street food market with local specialities

explanation.body: Suche die **Schlüsselwörter** in der Personenbeschreibung und finde sie im Angebot wieder: *animals, nature* → Zoo, park · *history, old buildings* → museum, palace · *local dishes, street food* → street food market · *music, live show* → concert.
In der Prüfung gibt es meist 5 Personen und 7 Angebote, jede Person bekommt **zwei** Angebote, und ein Angebot kann **mehrfach** passen. Arbeite mit den Schlüsselwörtern, nicht mit dem Gefühl.

subject: EN
prompt:
Read the sign. What does it say?

**{{s_sign}}**

explanation.body: Bei Schildern zählt die **Aussage**, nicht ein einzelnes Wort. Lies alle vier Antworten, es ist **genau eine** richtig. Achte auf Verbote (*do not, no …*), Warnungen (*danger, beware, careful*) und Bedingungen (*only, unless, before*).

source: Eigene Übungsaufgaben nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading 2: Schilder und Kurztexte)

from.sign: Please do not touch the plants. They are delicate and may not survive.
from.grund: *do not touch* + *plants* → Berühren verboten.

from.sign: DANGER. The rocks are extremely slippery. Several people have been injured while climbing here.
from.a: Do not climb on the rocks
from.grund: *slippery* + *injured while climbing* → das Klettern ist gefährlich, also nicht klettern.

from.sign: WiFi password? Send Mum a photo of the clean kitchen first.
from.a: The children have to clean the kitchen before they get the WiFi password
from.b: Mum wants to teach her children photography
from.c: Mum has left the house and wants a photo
from.grund: *clean kitchen first* → erst aufräumen, dann Passwort.

from.sign: Zeb the monkey throws objects. His aim is very accurate.
from.a: Be careful, this animal could hit you
from.c: This animal is scared of visitors
from.grund: *throws objects* + *accurate aim* → er trifft, also Vorsicht.

from.sign: Café closed on Mondays. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 8 am – 6 pm.
from.a: You cannot get a coffee here on Monday
from.b: The café is open every day
from.d: The café is closed at the weekend
from.grund: *closed on Mondays* → montags gibt es keinen Kaffee.

from.sign: LOST: black cat, answers to the name Milo. Reward! Call 0176 …
from.a: Someone is looking for their cat
from.d: A cat has found a new home
from.grund: *lost*, *reward*, *call* → jemand sucht sein Haustier.

from.sign: Bike parking only. Cars will be towed away at the owner's expense.
from.a: Cars are not allowed to park here
from.d: You can buy a bike here
from.grund: *bike parking only* + *cars will be towed* → Autos werden abgeschleppt.

from.sign: The worst coffee one woman on Tripadvisor ever had in her life.
from.a: The café makes fun of a bad online review
from.c: Only women are allowed in the café
from.d: The café says other cafés are worse
from.grund: Das Schild zitiert ironisch eine schlechte Bewertung (*Tripadvisor*), um Kunden anzulocken.

from.sign: Library quiet zone. Phones on silent, no food, no group work.
from.a: You have to be quiet in this area
from.b: You can eat here if you are quiet
from.c: Group work is allowed with permission
from.d: Phones are not allowed in the library
from.grund: *quiet zone* + Verbote → Ruhe; Handys sind erlaubt, aber stumm.

from.sign: Last entry 4:30 pm. The museum closes at 5 pm.
from.a: You cannot go in after 4:30 pm
from.grund: *last entry* = letzter Einlass.

subject: EN
prompt:
**Why some teenagers are switching off**

(1) Fifteen-year-old Amira from Leeds used to spend more than five hours a day on her phone. (2) "I didn't even notice," she says. (3) "I just kept scrolling." (4) In January she joined a school project called *Offline Hours*: for one month, students agreed to keep their phones in a box between 7 pm and 9 pm. (5) At first, Amira felt nervous and bored. (6) After a week, she started reading again and even called her grandmother instead of texting her. (7) A survey at the end of the project showed that 70 per cent of the students slept better and 60 per cent felt less stressed. (8) Only a few said the project had changed nothing. (9) The school now wants to offer *Offline Hours* every term, and Amira has kept her own rule: no phone after 8 pm. (10) "My friends thought I was crazy," she laughs. (11) "Now three of them do it too."

**1. What was Amira's problem before the project?**

choices: She used her phone for many hours without noticing it.
She had no phone and felt left out.
Her grandmother did not answer her calls.
She could not sleep because of her homework.

solution.correct_choice: She used her phone for many hours without noticing it.

explanation.title: Beleg
explanation.body: Sätze 1 bis 3: *more than five hours a day* und *I didn't even notice … I just kept scrolling*.
Schlüsselwörter der Frage (*problem, before*) → Textanfang. Die richtige Antwort steht meist **in anderen Worten** im Text.

source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading 3: Artikel)

subject: EN
prompt:
**Why some teenagers are switching off** (text see above)

**2. What did the students have to do during *Offline Hours*?**

choices: Put their phones away for two hours every evening for a month
Give their phones to the school for a month

solution.correct_choice: Put their phones away for two hours every evening for a month

explanation.title: Beleg
explanation.body: Satz 4: *for one month … keep their phones in a box between 7 pm and 9 pm*. Zwei Stunden pro Abend, nicht den ganzen Tag, nicht für immer.

source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch

subject: EN
prompt:
**Why some teenagers are switching off** (text see above)

**3. Which statement about the survey is correct?**

choices: Most students slept better and many felt less stressed.
The project changed nothing for most students.
60 per cent of the students slept better.

solution.correct_choice: Most students slept better and many felt less stressed.

explanation.title: Beleg
explanation.body: Satz 7: *70 per cent … slept better and 60 per cent felt less stressed*. Satz 8: *Only a few said the project had changed nothing.* Achte auf die Zahlen: 70 = schlafen, 60 = Stress.
Falle: Zahlen vertauscht (*60 per cent slept better*) oder übertrieben (*all students*).

source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch

subject: EN
prompt:
**Why some teenagers are switching off** (text see above)

**4. What does the last paragraph (sentences 9–11) tell us?**

choices: Amira still limits her phone use and some friends have copied her.
Amira stopped the rule because her friends laughed at her.
The school has cancelled the project.
Amira's friends never use their phones now.

solution.correct_choice: Amira still limits her phone use and some friends have copied her.

explanation.title: Beleg
explanation.body: Satz 9: *Amira has kept her own rule*. Satz 11: *Now three of them do it too.* Die Schule will das Projekt sogar **jedes Halbjahr** anbieten (Satz 9).

subject: EN
prompt:
Read the paragraph. Which words are the **keywords** that tell you the topic?

*This year, selfie sticks were banned at several music festivals. In some countries, using a selfie stick in dangerous places can even lead to arrest, after fatal accidents happened when people took selfies in front of trains.*

choices: selfie sticks, banned, arrest, dangerous, accidents
this year, several, some, even, when

solution.correct_choice: selfie sticks, banned, arrest, dangerous, accidents

explanation.body: Schlüsselwörter sind meist **Nomen, die sich wiederholen** und mit dem Thema zusammenhängen. Hier: *selfie sticks* (zweimal), *banned, arrest, dangerous, accidents* → Thema: **die Gefahren von Selfie-Sticks**.
Markiere Schlüsselwörter im Text **und** in den Fragen. So findest du die Stelle mit der gesuchten Information in Sekunden.

source: Nach Prüfungshefte MSA Englisch Berlin 2026, Reading (Exkurs Schlüssel- und Signalwörter), eigener Text
